The shapes of four different complexes, $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$, are shown in Table 5.1.

The symbol $\mathbf{J}$ represents an atom or ion of a transition element.

The symbol $\mathbf{L}$ is used to represent a monodentate ligand.

Table 5.1

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Label **one** bond angle on **each** of complexes $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$, and identify the size of the angle in degrees.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify the shapes of complexes $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Two $\mathbf{L}$ ligands are exchanged with two **different** monodentate ligands $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ in each of complexes $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$, $\mathbf{R}$ and $\mathbf{S}$.

Identify all the complexes which form new complexes that show geometrical isomerism.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Three $\mathbf{L}$ ligands are exchanged with three **different** monodentate ligands $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$ in each of complexes $\mathbf{P}$, $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$.

Identify all the complexes which form new complexes that show optical isomerism.
